walkthroughs.body_html:
Stellar Properties & Classification — a core area of A-Level Astronomy.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Stellar Properties & Classification brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Stellar Properties & Classification.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What is the full MK class of the Sun?
options: G0V
G2V
K5III
M0V

mcqs.q: Class V denotes which type of star?
options: Supergiant
Giant
Main sequence
White dwarf

mcqs.q: What defines a star as being on the 'main sequence'?
options: It is the largest stage of a star's life.
It fuses hydrogen into helium in its core.
It is the hottest stage.
Whether it has planets.

mcqs.q: What determines whether a star becomes a white dwarf or a neutron star?
options: Its colour during its main sequence phase.
Its mass - low/medium mass becomes a white dwarf; massive stars produce neutron stars or black holes.
It is the hottest stage.
Whether it has planets.

mcqs.q: Why are Type Ia supernovae used as 'standard candles'?
options: Because they happen at regular time intervals.
Because they are the brightest objects in the universe.
They have nearly uniform peak brightness, so their apparent brightness reveals distance.
Whether it has planets.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Metallicity”?
options: Temperature of an equivalent black body radiating the same total flux as the star.
Roman numerals I-VII labelling supergiant (I), giant (III), main sequence (V), white dwarf (VII).
Adds luminosity class to spectral type (e.g., G2V for the Sun); standard since 1943.
Abundance of elements heavier than helium; affects opacity, evolution and population type.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Morgan-Keenan system”?
options: Abundance of elements heavier than helium; affects opacity, evolution and population type.
Roman numerals I-VII labelling supergiant (I), giant (III), main sequence (V), white dwarf (VII).
Adds luminosity class to spectral type (e.g., G2V for the Sun); standard since 1943.
Temperature of an equivalent black body radiating the same total flux as the star.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Luminosity class”?
options: Original system devised at Harvard Observatory, ordering stars by hydrogen-line strength.
Temperature of an equivalent black body radiating the same total flux as the star.
Roman numerals I-VII labelling supergiant (I), giant (III), main sequence (V), white dwarf (VII).
OBAFGKM letters based on stellar spectra; correlates strongly with surface temperature.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Spectral type”?
options: OBAFGKM letters based on stellar spectra; correlates strongly with surface temperature.
Roman numerals I-VII labelling supergiant (I), giant (III), main sequence (V), white dwarf (VII).
Temperature of an equivalent black body radiating the same total flux as the star.
Original system devised at Harvard Observatory, ordering stars by hydrogen-line strength.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Harvard classification”?
options: Adds luminosity class to spectral type (e.g., G2V for the Sun); standard since 1943.
Original system devised at Harvard Observatory, ordering stars by hydrogen-line strength.
Abundance of elements heavier than helium; affects opacity, evolution and population type.
OBAFGKM letters based on stellar spectra; correlates strongly with surface temperature.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Effective temperature”?
options: Roman numerals I-VII labelling supergiant (I), giant (III), main sequence (V), white dwarf (VII).
Adds luminosity class to spectral type (e.g., G2V for the Sun); standard since 1943.
OBAFGKM letters based on stellar spectra; correlates strongly with surface temperature.
Temperature of an equivalent black body radiating the same total flux as the star.
